conventions.convention: Vertex charges lie in the strict upper half-plane; phase is principal argument divided by π. Semistability requires every nonzero subobject to have phase at most that of the ambient object. Zero is included without a phase.

Hall multiplication is subobject-first and counts distinct embedded subobjects separately. Phase factors are multiplied with the largest phase leftmost, in the dimension completion; products are degreewise formal.

Euler integration weights by inverse automorphism order and uses twist q^(-χ(e,d)). Skew integration additionally weights degree d by t^(χ(d,d)), where t=√q>0, and uses twist t^(-〈e,d〉), with 〈d,e〉=χ(d,e)-χ(e,d).

Motivic convolution is quotient-first; the referenced rational Borel–Moore CoHA is subobject-first with intrinsic group-dimension regrading and degree shift -2χ(b,a). Critical coefficients and integration require separately specified data and results. The referenced CoHA constructions assume AC.
Finite-field Hall generators are mathematical invariants; neither a CY3/CoHA bridge nor a physical protected-state identification is asserted to exist.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite acyclic quiver over F_q with upper-half-plane vertex charges, define P_Z^E as the decreasing-phase product of I(S_Z(φ)) and P_Z^sk as the decreasing-phase skew product of J(S_Z(φ)), in their respective dimension completions.

For any finite acyclic quiver over F_q, without a finite-representation-type restriction, and any two upper-half-plane vertex-charge assignments Z_- and Z_+, P_(Z_-)^E=P_(Z_+)^E and P_(Z_-)^sk=P_(Z_+)^sk. Each generator is a unit with constant term 1 and the equal generators induce equal continuous conjugation automorphisms of the corresponding completed torus.

concerns.concern: Fact F1 states: “a nonzero subrepresentation is semistable precisely when its phase is at most the phase of the whole representation.” This is false as written and misstates def-finite-acyclic-quiver-stability-data. For φ1>φ2, take the ambient representation M0 and its subrepresentation S1: S1 is stable, although φ(S1)>φ(M0). The supplier instead says that the ambient representation is semistable precisely when every nonzero subrepresentation satisfies the phase inequality. Verification step 3.1 uses that correct ambient-object criterion, so this finding concerns the explicit Fact rather than the displayed Hall coefficients or chamber calculation.
